identification: Three Tasmanian pottery pieces: small ribbed turquoise-green pot incised 'B333/B535 John Campbell Tasmania' (John Campbell Pottery, Launceston, c1930s); larger green drip-glaze vase, glazed base, unmarked (Campbell style, chip to foot rim); blue Tasmania-map pin dish incised 'Launceston Tas.' and 'By Robert Campbell Launceston' (probably a Campbell family or amateur piece, not a listed Campbell Pottery mark; no Robert Campbell pottery found online).

entries.note: John Campbell baluster mottled-glaze vase, 9.5cm, incised John Campbell Launceston. Comparable in size to the small pot. From local comps database (not opened by me). Hammer, premium extra.
John Campbell blue glazed trough, 31cm wide; larger, better form than the dish. From comps database. Hammer.

John Campbell squat two-handled green drip-glaze vase with incised band, results $200 (May 2025), $260 (Dec 2024), $160, $200, $260 (Nov 2025). Better and larger than the unmarked green vase here; good condition assumed. From comps database. Median $200.
Two-handled bulbous green drip vase incised John Campbell Tasmania, glaze chip noted; a bigger, better piece. From comps database. Hammer.
Signed John Campbell squat green/orange drip vase, 8cm, with base repair. Closest to a damaged small piece. From comps database.
John Campbell pottery vase, signed, 4 bids. Paid locally: shows what we might pay, not a resale price.
Mixed ceramics incl Martin Boyd and John Campbell, some damage. Paid locally, not resale.

viewing_check: Check the larger green vase base and sides for any incised John Campbell mark or number; inspect the chip to the foot rim and the glaze flake on the small pot; confirm the 'By Robert Campbell' dish mark and whether it is pressed or hand incised. Look for hairlines.
